annotation.title_clean: Legal regulation of artificial intelligence and robotic systems: review of key approaches
annotation.title_en: Legal regulation of artificial intelligence and robotic systems: review of key approaches
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kuteynikov, D.; Izhaev, O.; Lebedev, V.; Zenin, S.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article comparing legal regulation of AI and robotic systems in the EU (risk-based draft AI Act), the US (fragmented, ad hoc, sectoral) and China (New Generation AI Development Plan). It concludes AI policies protect citizens' rights across fields, noting trade-offs between regulatory burden and innovation.
key_provisions_or_claims: EU draft AI Act uses a risk-based, person-centred approach but may slow industry growth.
US has no cross-cutting AI law; ad hoc sectoral regulation favours economic growth but risks incidents.
China relies on the New Generation AI Development Plan, with associated political risks.
US 2020 OMB memorandum sets principles favouring non-regulatory approaches.
